title.value: Enantioselective Synthesis of Both Enantiomers of Chiral Allenes Using Chiral N-Methylcamphanyl Piperazine Templates

abstract.value: Allenes are versatile functional groups that could act as useful synthons for synthetic manipulations, with the potential for conversion to chiral molecules with asymmetric centers.<sup>[1]</sup> Chiral allene structural motifs are also present in several biologically active natural products and pharmaceuticals.<sup>[2]</sup> For decades, chiral allenes have been prepared by the general reaction of propargyl alcohol derivatives with nucleophiles by $\mathrm { S } _ { \mathrm { N } } 2$ addition. Generally, the methods available to access enantiomerically enriched allenes require multi-step synthetic operations.<sup>[3]</sup> Metal-catalysed enantioselective synthesis of chiral allenes from chiral propargylamines using gold<sup>[4a]</sup> and silver(I)<sup>[4b]</sup> complexes and zinc halides<sup>[4c]</sup> by a two-step synthetic protocol have been reported. Although the preparation of a monosubstituted allene from CuBr, a 1-alkyne, and formaldehyde was reported by Crabbe in 1979, the synthesis of racemic 1,3-disubstituted allenes from terminal alkynes, aldehydes, morpholine, and $\mathrm { Z n X } _ { 2 }$ was reported only very recently.<sup>[5]</sup> We have recently reported that zinc halides promote the one-pot enantioselective synthesis of chiral allenes using aldehydes, terminal alkynes, and the chiral amine derivatives (1–3; Scheme 1).<sup>[6]</sup>

value.ligand_or_chiral_source: prolinol-derived and other chiral amine catalysts
